stories.title: Kraken opens Bitcoin and Ethereum options to eligible European traders
stories.summary: Kraken launched options trading on Bitcoin and Ethereum for eligible traders in Europe. The move adds a new derivatives product to the exchange's regional lineup. CryptoSlate did not specify the exact eligibility rules or which countries get access first.
stories.whyItMatters: Wider regulated derivatives access in Europe shows major exchanges are deepening their product range there.
whatToWatch: Which European markets gain access first
Early trading volume on the new options
questions: What eligibility rules apply to traders?
Will Kraken add options on other assets next?

stories.title: OpenAI claims a cryptography breakthrough. Does it threaten Bitcoin?
stories.summary: OpenAI announced a cryptography breakthrough, and CryptoSlate raised the question of whether it threatens Bitcoin's security. The report frames this as an open question, not a confirmed risk. No technical details of the claimed breakthrough were given.
stories.whyItMatters: Bitcoin's security rests on cryptographic assumptions, so any claim that challenges them draws scrutiny, even when unproven.
whatToWatch: Technical details or peer review of OpenAI's claim
questions: What exactly did OpenAI claim to break?
Does the claim touch the cryptography Bitcoin actually uses?

stories.title: Analysis: a Bitcoin rally could push holders of 874,000 BTC to sell
stories.summary: A CryptoSlate analysis says a future Bitcoin rally could trigger selling from a group of holders who control about 874,000 BTC. The piece presents this as a possible scenario drawn from on-chain data, not a forecast. No price level or timeframe was given for when this might happen.
stories.whyItMatters: Large holder cohorts can shape how a rally unfolds, but readers should treat this as speculation, not a signal to act on.
whatToWatch: On-chain movement from this holder group if price rises
questions: How is this 874,000 BTC cohort defined?
How reliable is this kind of on-chain modeling?

sources.title: Bitcoin’s next rally could trigger selling from holders of 874,000 BTC

stories.title: Lightning Network tightens invoice rules after attack made withdrawals look unpaid
stories.summary: The Lightning Network tightened its invoice rules after a reported attack made some Bitcoin withdrawals appear unpaid when they had gone through. CryptoSlate reported the change as a direct response to the exploit. The report did not name the affected services or explain the attack's mechanics.
stories.whyItMatters: Lightning is Bitcoin's main payment layer, so a flaw in payment confirmation affects trust for wallets and merchants that rely on it.
whatToWatch: Adoption of the new rules across wallets and nodes
Further disclosure on which services were hit
questions: Which services or users were affected?
Does the fix need a coordinated upgrade across implementations?

sources.title: Lightning tightens invoice rules after reported attack made Bitcoin withdrawals look unpaid

stories.title: Ripple receives final US trust bank approval
stories.summary: Ripple received final approval for a US trust bank charter, CryptoSlate reported. This closes the last regulatory step in a process the company had pursued. The report treats the effect on XRP as an open question, not a settled outcome.
stories.whyItMatters: A trust bank charter lets Ripple hold and manage customer assets under federal oversight, a significant regulatory milestone for a major crypto firm.
whatToWatch: How Ripple uses the charter in its stablecoin and custody business
Any product changes tied to the approval
questions: What can Ripple now do that it could not before?
Does this have a direct effect on XRP's price or use?

sources.title: Ripple gets final US trust bank approval. What does XRP gain?

stories.title: Iran-linked Bitcoin activity fell 80%, then rebounded during a blackout
stories.summary: Iran-linked Bitcoin activity dropped by about 80% and then rebounded during a reported blackout, CryptoSlate said. The pattern points to a connectivity disruption that interrupted on-chain activity before it recovered. The report gave no further detail on the blackout's cause or length.
stories.whyItMatters: Bitcoin use in sanctioned or restricted jurisdictions stays a recurring concern for regulators and exchanges.
whatToWatch: Official confirmation of the blackout's cause
Further on-chain tracking of Iran-linked wallets
questions: How is 'Iran-linked' activity identified, and how reliable is that method?

stories.title: Bitcoin moved $5 billion on-chain while miners collected just $185,000 in fees
stories.summary: Bitcoin's network moved over $5 billion in value in a period where miners collected only about $185,000 in transaction fees, CryptoSlate reported. Separately, the outlet ran simulations suggesting a price return to $126,000 would not hold. The fee figure is a concrete data point; the price scenario is a model, not a forecast.
stories.whyItMatters: Low fee revenue against high transaction value matters for miner economics, while the price simulation is speculative and should not be read as a prediction.
whatToWatch: Miner fee trends if transaction volume stays high
questions: What is driving the low fee-to-value ratio?
What assumptions underlie the simulation's conclusion?

sources.title: Bitcoin simulations show why a return to $126,000 would not last
Bitcoin moves over $5 billion in value but miners collect just $185,000 in transaction fees

stories.title: Coinbase sets 3-day MiCA deadline for USDT, PayPal, and Trump-linked stablecoins
stories.summary: Coinbase set a three-day deadline tied to MiCA compliance for stablecoins including USDT, PayPal's stablecoin, and a Trump-linked stablecoin, CryptoSlate reported. The deadline suggests these tokens face restriction on Coinbase's European platform if they miss EU rules in time. The report did not specify the exact compliance gap or Coinbase's planned action after the deadline.
stories.whyItMatters: MiCA enforcement is reshaping which stablecoins exchanges can offer in the EU, directly affecting liquidity and access to major tokens like USDT.
whatToWatch: Coinbase's action once the 3-day deadline passes
Whether issuers reach MiCA compliance in time
questions: What MiCA requirement are these stablecoins failing to meet?
Will other EU exchanges set similar deadlines?

sources.title: Coinbase sets 3-day MiCA deadline for USDT, PayPal and Trump-linked stablecoins

stories.title: Japan's split services inflation complicates the BOJ outlook before Friday's decision
stories.summary: A split in Japan's services inflation data is complicating the outlook for the Bank of Japan ahead of its policy decision on Friday, CryptoSlate reported. The report did not specify the direction of the split or the decision markets expect.
stories.whyItMatters: BOJ policy shifts affect global liquidity and risk appetite, which can spill over into crypto markets.
whatToWatch: The Bank of Japan's policy decision on Friday
questions: What is driving the divergence in services inflation?
How might the BOJ's decision affect crypto and other risk assets?
